engine.name: A.R.I.A. Attention Engine
engine.purpose: Determine which active work items should be surfaced to a user at a given moment, which should remain visible but non-interruptive, which should be deferred, and which should remain quietly monitored. The engine converts operational priority into useful attention without overwhelming the user.
principles: Priority and attention are related but distinct.
High-priority work does not always require immediate interruption.
Attention is contextual to the user, time, current circumstances, and actionability.
A.R.I.A. should protect the user from both forgotten obligations and unnecessary noise.
The purpose of attention management is not to display everything that exists.
The purpose of attention management is to surface what is useful to deal with now.
Work that cannot currently be acted upon should not repeatedly consume attention without reason.
Small actions that prevent future escalation may deserve attention before larger but non-actionable work.
A materially changed condition may justify resurfacing an item.
Snoozing changes presentation timing, not the underlying truth or priority of the work.
Delegated and waiting work may require attention when intervention or follow-up becomes appropriate.
Strategic work must receive deliberate attention opportunities so recurring emergencies do not eliminate it indefinitely.

requirements: The latest available priority evaluation should be used when practical.
Stale priority may trigger reevaluation before an attention decision.
Attention evaluation must not silently alter authoritative source facts.
User context may affect presentation but must not redefine the underlying operational truth.

rules: Inactive work items should not appear in ordinary current-attention results.
A waiting item remains eligible when follow-up, escalation, verification, or intervention is appropriate.
A delegated item remains eligible when oversight or follow-up is appropriate.
A blocked item remains eligible when the user can remove or influence the blocker.
A scheduled item may remain quiet until preparation or action becomes useful.
Captured items with unresolved interpretation may be surfaced when clarification from the user is materially necessary.

interrupt.description: Surface immediately or at the earliest appropriate interruption point because delay is likely to create substantial consequence.
examples: major blocker requiring the user's direct action
time-sensitive opportunity likely to be lost

now.description: Present as work the user should reasonably address in the current working period.
examples: short action that prevents likely escalation

soon.description: Keep prominently visible for upcoming attention but do not displace more consequential current work.
examples: preparation required for a future obligation

watch.description: Keep active and monitor without routinely consuming the user's attention.
examples: monitoring condition with no current intervention required

deferred.description: Intentionally suppress ordinary presentation until a defined condition or time while preserving the work item.
examples: item not actionable until a known future date

clarify.description: Surface because a small amount of user input is materially necessary to correctly handle the work.
examples: unclear whether an obligation was accepted

priority.description: Current operational priority score, band, factors, and reason.

actionability.description: Whether meaningful action can be taken by the target user now.

consequence_of_delay.description: Expected consequence if the item is not addressed during the relevant attention window.

deadline_proximity.description: Proximity and consequence of applicable deadlines or commitments.

follow_up_state.description: Whether follow-up is currently appropriate, due, or overdue.

blocking_effect.description: Whether the user's action would unblock other people, systems, projects, or work.

waiting_state.description: Whether the item is legitimately waiting and whether intervention is now useful.

delegation_state.description: Whether another party owns the next action and whether oversight is currently required.

material_change.description: Whether new information has materially changed the item's significance or required action.

strategic_value.description: Whether the item requires protected attention despite lacking immediate urgency.

presentation_history.description: Whether the item has recently been surfaced and whether repeating it would add value.

snooze_state.description: Whether presentation has intentionally been deferred.

user_availability.description: Whether the user is reasonably available for the type of attention being considered.

required_effort.description: Approximate effort required for the next meaningful action when that information is available.

rules: Actionability affects presentation but does not directly redefine priority.
A critical non-actionable item may remain under active monitoring without repeated interruption.
A low-effort action that prevents a high-consequence future problem may warrant immediate attention.
Unknown actionability should not automatically be interpreted as actionable.

interruption_policy.purpose: Prevent A.R.I.A. from becoming another source of constant distraction.
rules: Interrupt only when the expected value of immediate awareness materially exceeds the cost of interruption.
Critical priority alone does not require interruption when no meaningful user action is possible.
Interruptions should identify what changed, why it matters now, and what action is available.
Repeated interruption for the same unchanged condition should be avoided.
A materially worsening condition may justify renewed interruption.
Safety-critical or severe consequence conditions may override ordinary interruption suppression.
User-defined do-not-disturb or availability rules should be respected except where authorized escalation policy permits otherwise.

triggers: waiting duration exceeds expected response window
strategic work reaches protected review point
rules: Resurfacing should occur because circumstances justify renewed attention, not merely because time passed.
Aging may contribute to resurfacing when an obligation risks being forgotten.
Repeated unchanged resurfacing should be suppressed when it adds no value.
A user dismissal is not equivalent to completion unless the user explicitly resolves the underlying work.
Snooze suppresses ordinary presentation until a time or condition.
Snooze does not change work item status by itself.
Snooze does not reduce the underlying priority score merely because the user does not want to see the item.
A materially changed condition may override snooze when authorized by attention policy.
Snooze expiration requires reevaluation rather than automatic escalation.

strategic_attention.purpose: Prevent important non-urgent work from being permanently displaced by urgent operational demands.
rules: Strategically important work may receive protected attention windows.
Strategic work should not be falsely labeled urgent merely to keep it visible.
Repeated displacement of strategic work should increase its presentation significance without manufacturing a false deadline.
The system should distinguish urgent interruption from deliberate strategic focus.
Protected strategic attention should consider the user's actual availability.

clarification_policy.purpose: Ask the user only when their input materially improves operational handling.
rules: Do not ask for information that can be reliably obtained from authorized sources.
Do not ask the user to classify every captured item.
Ask when unresolved ambiguity materially affects ownership, timing, commitment, action, or consequence.
Prefer concise clarification questions.
Where safe and useful, preserve the work candidate and continue other processing while clarification is pending.
Clarification requests themselves should not become unnecessary recurring interruptions.

requirements: Tell the user what needs attention.
Explain why it needs attention now.
Identify the next meaningful action when known.
Identify important deadlines or commitments when relevant.
Identify what is blocking progress when relevant.
Avoid requiring the user to reconstruct the source history merely to understand the obligation.
Provide source context when it materially helps the user act or verify the recommendation.

daily_attention_view.purpose: Provide a concise operational view of what deserves the user's attention without presenting the entire work inventory.
rules: Sections may be omitted when empty.
The same item should not be unnecessarily repeated across sections.
The view should emphasize decisions and actions rather than raw message volume.
The view must not imply that omitted active work has been deleted or completed.
The user should be able to request the broader work inventory separately.

requirements: Attention decisions must reference the applicable work_item_id.
Attention state must not silently alter work item status.
Presentation ranking must not overwrite the Priority Engine's canonical score.
Material reasons for surfacing an item should be explainable.
Presentation history should be updated when an item is actually surfaced.

rules: The Priority Engine determines current operational priority.
The Attention Engine determines whether, when, and how that priority should consume user attention.
The Attention Engine may request priority reevaluation when the existing evaluation is stale or circumstances changed.
The Attention Engine must not independently replace the canonical priority score.
The Capture Engine determines whether operational work exists.
The Attention Engine does not create work merely because information is interesting.
A clarification need discovered during attention evaluation may be returned to capture or workflow handling when the underlying work item requires correction.

guardrails: Do not show every active work item as urgent.
Do not interrupt merely because an item exists.
Do not equate priority with interruption.
Do not repeatedly surface unchanged non-actionable work.
Do not allow waiting work to disappear.
Do not allow delegated work to disappear.
Do not allow strategic work to disappear indefinitely.
Do not treat snooze as completion.
Do not reduce objective priority solely because an item was snoozed.
Do not assume the user must personally perform every important action.
Do not ask unnecessary clarification questions.
Do not overwrite canonical priority during presentation ranking.
Do not modify Core reasoning architecture as part of attention management.
